name: Timers (every, after)
summary: Engine timers: `every` fires a rule at a constant interval; `after` schedules a one-shot event after any int-ms expression (self-rescheduling after-timers make ramps).
when_to_use: Spawning on a beat, delayed reveals, cooldowns, speed ramps that need a changing interval.
api: timers: every <const ms> | after <int-ms expr>; time_limit is a constant
notes: every and time_limit take constants only; after takes expressions

name: Tick rules
summary: Rules that run every step at a fixed 60 Hz with dt, for movement, custom collisions and accumulators.
when_to_use: Any custom real-time movement or check not covered by a fragment.
api: rules on tick; dt in ms; collisions are expressions in tick rules

name: Physics bodies
summary: Optional engine physics: circle or axis-aligned box bodies on state records, gravity, bounds with bounce, max speed, solid collisions with a contact normal, and collision and bounds events.
when_to_use: Falling, bouncing, stacking-on-top and landing mechanics: ball games, simple platformers, drop-and-stack. Not rotation, joints or segments (see gaps).
api: "physics": {gravity: [x, y], bounds: [x, y, w, h], bodies: {group: {state, static?, bounded?, bounce?, gravity?, max_speed?}}, collisions: [{a, b, solid?, emit}], on_bounds: [{body, emit}]}; emit payload a, b, nx, ny
notes: engine v0.2; no fragment wraps it yet; shapes are circles and unrotated boxes only

name: Camera
summary: A camera that offsets the world view (x, y as expressions), with fixed HUD nodes; hit-testing and pointers use world coordinates.
when_to_use: Side-scrollers, tall towers, big maps and runners whose world is larger than one screen.
api: "presentation": {"camera": {"x": "= expr", "y": "= expr"}}; nodes with "fixed": true ignore it

name: Hold buttons
summary: Nodes that send an input on pointer down and another on release, for hold-to-move controls and charge-up mechanics.
when_to_use: Hold to charge, hold to move with on-screen buttons, hold-and-release timing games.
api: node props on_press / on_release {input, with}; pattern in engine/examples/lantern_ridge.json

name: Pointer input
summary: Canvas-wide pointer down, up and move sources (move only while down), in world coordinates, plus on_tap and on_drag nodes.
when_to_use: Swipes, slingshot pulls, aiming, tracing paths and drag gestures not tied to a node.
api: inputs.<name>.from: {"pointer": "down" | "up" | "move"} with pointer {x, y}; node on_tap / on_drag
notes: engine v0.2; one pointer at a time (see multi_touch gap)

name: Key input
summary: Hardware key sources: a named key or any key, down or up, with code and printable char.
when_to_use: Desktop and web-player controls, and as a second source next to on-screen controls.

name: Lines and polygons
summary: Line and polygon nodes (up to 256 points) besides rect, circle and text, for drawn paths, ropes, graphs and shapes.
when_to_use: Drawing a traced path, a trajectory preview, a maze wall, a chart or a custom silhouette.
api: nodes line {x1, y1, x2, y2, stroke, stroke_width}, poly {points, closed, fill, stroke}
notes: engine v0.2; drawing only, no collision against them

name: Image and sprite assets
summary: Image nodes with asset ids, sprite-sheet frames, flip, rotation and scale; the game's art roles fill fragment sprites.
when_to_use: Any game with drawn characters, tiles, cards or backgrounds (the art pipeline makes them).
api: node image {asset, w, h, frame, flip_x, flip_y, rotation, scale}; art roles avatar, hazard, pickup, tile, card, ...
notes: engine v0.2; bots tap rect/circle ops, so sprites need a transparent rect under them

name: Particles and haptics
summary: Feedback actions: seeded particle bursts and haptics (light to heavy, success, warning, error), plus conditional feedback.
when_to_use: Juice for hits, pickups, merges and wins in any game.
api: feedback {particles: {x, y, count, color, speed, size, ms, gravity, spread}} | {haptic: light | medium | heavy | success | warning | error}

name: Synth sound and music
summary: Sound feedback as samples, synth notes with slides, or note jingles, plus a looping music asset; note pitch can come from an expression.
when_to_use: Rhythm and music-making games, and sound moments in any game.
api: feedback {sound: {asset} | {wave, note, ms, slide} | {wave, notes, step_ms}}; presentation.music {asset, volume, playing}

name: Wrapped and outlined text
summary: Text nodes that wrap to a box width and can carry an outline stroke.
when_to_use: Story text, prompts, long questions and readable labels over busy art.

name: English dictionary
summary: The engine's built-in English word list, checked case-insensitively with in_dictionary(word).
when_to_use: Word games that accept any real word: anagrams, word chains, boggle-like grids, spelling bees.
